claim: Synaptotagmin-1 (Syt1) acts as a Ca2+ sensor for neurotransmitter release through its C2 domains.
source: Synaptotagmin-1 (Syt1) acts as a Ca2+ sensor for neurotransmitter release through its C2 domains.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: It has been proposed that Syt1 promotes SNARE-dependent fusion mainly through its C2B domain.
source: It has been proposed that Syt1 promotes SNARE-dependent fusion mainly through its C2B domain, but the underlying mechanism is poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated as a proposition from prior work, indicating citation-based support.

claim: The C2B domain interacts simultaneously with acidic membranes and SNARE complexes via the top Ca2+-binding loops, the side polybasic patch, and the bottom face in response to Ca2+.
source: In this study, we show that the C2B domain interacts simultaneously with acidic membranes and SNARE complexes via the top Ca2+-binding loops, the side polybasic patch, and the bottom face in response to Ca2+.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Disruption of the simultaneous interactions completely abrogates the triggering activity of the C2B domain in liposome fusion.
source: Disruption of the simultaneous interactions completely abrogates the triggering activity of the C2B domain in liposome fusion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from liposome fusion assays shown in Figure 7.

claim: The simultaneous interactions endow the C2B domain with an ability to deform local membranes.
source: We hypothesize that the simultaneous interactions endow the C2B domain with an ability to deform local membranes, and this membrane-deformation activity might underlie the functional significance of the Syt1 C2B domain in vivo.
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: The core machinery governing Ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter release includes the SNAREs synaptobrevin, syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25.
source: The core machinery governing the process includes the SNAREs synaptobrevin, syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25, which form tight SNARE complexes to bridge synaptic vesicles to the plasma membrane and catalyze membrane fusion (Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Sutton et al., 1998; Weber et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: SNAREs form tight SNARE complexes to bridge synaptic vesicles to the plasma membrane and catalyze membrane fusion.
source: The core machinery governing the process includes the SNAREs synaptobrevin, syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25, which form tight SNARE complexes to bridge synaptic vesicles to the plasma membrane and catalyze membrane fusion (Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Sutton et al., 1998; Weber et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Syt1 is the Ca2+ sensor for the fast component of Ca2+-triggered release.
source: Syt1, the Ca2+ sensor for the fast component of Ca2+-triggered release (Chapman, 2008; Fernandez-Chacon et al., 2001; Geppert et al., 1994), confers Ca2+ sensitivity to SNARE-dependent synaptic vesicle fusion.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Syt1 confers Ca2+ sensitivity to SNARE-dependent synaptic vesicle fusion.
source: Syt1, the Ca2+ sensor for the fast component of Ca2+-triggered release (Chapman, 2008; Fernandez-Chacon et al., 2001; Geppert et al., 1994), confers Ca2+ sensitivity to SNARE-dependent synaptic vesicle fusion.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The triggering function of Syt1 depends on its interplay with membranes, SNAREs, complexins and other key proteins of the release machinery.
source: The triggering function of Syt1 depends on its interplay with membranes, SNAREs, complexins and other key proteins of the release machinery (Rizo and Xu, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Syt1 consists of two C2 domains, known as C2A and C2B.
source: Syt1 consists of two C2 domains, known as C2A and C2B.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Syt1.

claim: The C2A and C2B domains adopt similar structures.
source: The C2A and C2B domains adopt similar structures and bind three and two Ca2+ ions, respectively, through their Ca2+-binding loops located at the top of the structures (Fernandez et al., 2001; Shao et al., 1998; Sutton et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citations.

claim: C2A binds three Ca2+ ions through its Ca2+-binding loops.
source: The C2A and C2B domains adopt similar structures and bind three and two Ca2+ ions, respectively, through their Ca2+-binding loops located at the top of the structures (Fernandez et al., 2001; Shao et al., 1998; Sutton et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citations.

claim: C2B binds two Ca2+ ions through its Ca2+-binding loops.
source: The C2A and C2B domains adopt similar structures and bind three and two Ca2+ ions, respectively, through their Ca2+-binding loops located at the top of the structures (Fernandez et al., 2001; Shao et al., 1998; Sutton et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Ca2+-binding loops of Syt1 C2 domains are located at the top of the structures.
source: The C2A and C2B domains adopt similar structures and bind three and two Ca2+ ions, respectively, through their Ca2+-binding loops located at the top of the structures (Fernandez et al., 2001; Shao et al., 1998; Sutton et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Ca2+-binding loops mediate penetration of Syt1 C2 domains to acidic membranes containing phosphatidylserine (PS) in response to Ca2+.
source: These loops mediate penetration of Syt1 C2 domains to acidic membranes containing phosphatidylserine (PS) in response to Ca2+, and this activity is required for the triggering function of Syt1 (Chapman and Davis, 1998; Fernandez-Chacon et al., 2001; Rhee et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The membrane penetration activity of Syt1 C2 domains is required for the triggering function of Syt1.
source: These loops mediate penetration of Syt1 C2 domains to acidic membranes containing phosphatidylserine (PS) in response to Ca2+, and this activity is required for the triggering function of Syt1 (Chapman and Davis, 1998; Fernandez-Chacon et al., 2001; Rhee et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Syt1 readily binds to phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) via its C2B domain in a Ca2+-independent manner.
source: In addition, Syt1 readily binds to phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) via its C2B domain in a Ca2+-independent manner, which helps increase the apparent Ca2+ affinity of Syt1 and thereby enhances release probability (Bai et al., 2004; Li et al., 2006; Radhakrishnan et al., 2009; van den Bogaart et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 binding to C2B helps increase the apparent Ca2+ affinity of Syt1 and thereby enhances release probability.
source: In addition, Syt1 readily binds to phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) via its C2B domain in a Ca2+-independent manner, which helps increase the apparent Ca2+ affinity of Syt1 and thereby enhances release probability (Bai et al., 2004; Li et al., 2006; Radhakrishnan et al., 2009; van den Bogaart et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Syt1 binds to SNAP-25 and syntaxin-1, and to SNARE complexes mainly through its C2B domain.
source: Furthermore, Syt1 binds to SNAP-25 and syntaxin-1, and to SNARE complexes mainly through its C2B domain, which is believed to position Syt1 on the pre-fusion SNARE complexes to trigger release in response to Ca2+ (Brewer et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015; de Wit et al., 2009; Mohrmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: C2B binding to SNAREs is believed to position Syt1 on the pre-fusion SNARE complexes to trigger release in response to Ca2+.
source: Furthermore, Syt1 binds to SNAP-25 and syntaxin-1, and to SNARE complexes mainly through its C2B domain, which is believed to position Syt1 on the pre-fusion SNARE complexes to trigger release in response to Ca2+ (Brewer et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015; de Wit et al., 2009; Mohrmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Disrupting Ca2+ binding to C2B impairs release much more strongly than disruption of C2A Ca2+ binding sites in vivo.
source: It has been found that disrupting Ca2+ binding to C2B impairs release much more strongly than disruption of C2A Ca2+ binding sites in vivo (Mackler et al., 2002; Nishiki and Augustine, 2004; Robinson et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge from in vivo studies, supported by citations.

claim: Isolated C2B, instead of C2A, can promote SNARE-dependent membrane fusion in response to Ca2+ in vitro.
source: Moreover, previous work showed that isolated C2B, instead of C2A, can promote SNARE-dependent membrane fusion in response to Ca2+ in vitro (Gaffaney et al., 2008; Xue et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from in vitro studies, supported by citations.

claim: C2B plays a more preponderant role than C2A in neurotransmitter release.
source: These findings suggested that C2B plays a more preponderant role than C2A in neurotransmitter release.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited findings.

claim: The functional importance of C2B arises partly from its ability to deform membranes.
source: A number of studies have revisited this issue and suggested that the functional importance of C2B arises partly from its ability to deform membranes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from the literature.

claim: C2B can induce vesicle clustering and/or membrane curvature in response to Ca2+.
source: For instance, C2B can induce vesicle clustering and/or membrane curvature in response to Ca2+ (Arac et al., 2006; Martens et al., 2007; Hui et al., 2009; Xue et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Interactions between C2B and SNARE complexes are crucial for the function of Syt1 in neurotransmitter release.
source: Another potential reason for the striking functional asymmetry of the Syt1 C2 domains was provided by recent studies showing that interactions between C2B and SNARE complexes are crucial for the function of Syt1 in neurotransmitter release (Zhou et al., 2015; Brewer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A Syt1–SNARE complex crystal structure showed a binding interface involving Arg398 and Arg399 on the bottom of C2B.
source: For instance, a recently solved Syt1–SNARE complex crystal structure showed a relatively large binding interface between Syt1 and the SNARE complex that involves two basic residues (Arg398 and Arg399, referred to as the R398 R399 region, see Figure 1A) on the bottom of C2B (Zhou et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a structural finding from a cited study.

claim: A dynamic Syt1–SNARE complex structure model obtained by NMR indicated a SNARE binding interface located on the polybasic patch (Lys326 and Lys327) at the side of C2B.
source: whereas another dynamic Syt1–SNARE complex structure model obtained by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) indicated a SNARE binding interface that is located on the polybasic patch (Lys326 and Lys327, referred to as the K326 K327 region, see Figure 1A) at the side of C2B (Brewer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a structural finding from a cited study.

claim: Both the R398 R399 and K326 K327 regions have been implicated in binding to acidic membrane lipids, such as PS and PI(4,5)P2.
source: Moreover, both of these basic regions have been previously implicated in binding to acidic membrane lipids, such as PS and PI(4,5)P2 (Xue et al., 2008; van den Bogaart et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Some reports argued against the interaction between Syt1 and the SNARE complex, suggesting that the triggering function of Syt1 requires specific binding of C2B to acidic membranes rather than binding to SNARE complexes.
source: Some other reports argued against the interaction between Syt1 and the SNARE complex, and suggested that the triggering function of Syt1 requires specific binding of C2B to acidic membranes rather than binding to SNARE complexes (Honigmann et al., 2013; Park et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conflicting view from the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Both C2AB and C2B bound to assembled SNARE complexes, whereas C2A did not.
source: Consistent with previous results (Brewer et al., 2015), we found that both C2AB (soluble fragment of Syt1 harboring C2A and C2B) and C2B bound to assembled SNARE complexes, whereas C2A did not (Figure 2A,B, note that the C2A binding might be too weak to be detected on the gel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The SNARE complex containing the SNAP-25 D51A/E52A/E55A mutation showed impaired binding ability to C2B.
source: The SNARE complex containing the SNAP-25 D51A/E52A/E55A mutation (referred to as SN25 3M) showed impaired binding ability to C2B (Figure 2A,B), in agreement with previous findings (Brewer et al., 2015; Mohrmann et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B and is consistent with previous findings.

claim: Disruption of the C2B Ca2+-binding sites (D363N/D365N) caused no effect on the SNARE complex binding.
source: As expected, disruption of the C2B Ca2+-binding sites (D363N/D365N, referred to as C2b) caused no effect on the SNARE complex binding (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Disruption of either the K326 K327 region or the R398 R399 region impaired binding of C2B to the SNARE complex.
source: However, disruption of either the K326 K327 region or the R398 R399 region (K326A/K327A, K326E/K327E or R398Q/R399Q, referred to as C2B2KA, C2B2KE or C2B2RQ, respectively) impaired binding of C2B to the SNARE complex (Figure 2A,B), indicating that both basic regions of C2B contribute to the SNARE complex binding.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Both basic regions of C2B (K326 K327 and R398 R399) contribute to the SNARE complex binding.
source: However, disruption of either the K326 K327 region or the R398 R399 region (K326A/K327A, K326E/K327E or R398Q/R399Q, referred to as C2B2KA, C2B2KE or C2B2RQ, respectively) impaired binding of C2B to the SNARE complex (Figure 2A,B), indicating that both basic regions of C2B contribute to the SNARE complex binding.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Both C2AB and C2B (wild type) bound efficiently to liposomes containing 1% PI(4,5)P2 in the absence of Ca2+.
source: Using a liposome co-flotation assay (Figure 2C), we found that, in the absence of Ca2+, both C2AB and C2B (wild type, WT) bound efficiently to liposomes containing 1% PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The PI(4,5)P2-binding ability of Syt1 relies on the K326 K327 region but not the R398 R399 region.
source: This PI(4,5)P2-binding ability of Syt1 relies on the K326 K327 region but not the R398 R399 region, as C2AB2KE/C2AB2KA or C2B2KE/C2B2KA completely abolished binding to PI(4,5)P2-containing liposomes whereas C2AB2RQ or C2B2RQ did not (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: When NBD was placed close to the K326 K327 region (H315C-NBD), robust energy transfer was detected between C2B and PI(4,5)P2-containing liposomes in the absence of Ca2+.
source: When NBD was placed close to the K326 K327 region (H315C-NBD), we detected a robust energy transfer (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Ca2+-independent FRET signals were considerably weaker when PI(4,5)P2 was removed from liposomes.
source: Comparably, Ca2+-independent FRET signals were considerably weaker when PI(4,5)P2 was removed from liposomes (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: The addition of excess assembled SNARE complexes caused no obvious effect on the FRET between C2B and PI(4,5)P2-containing liposomes.
source: The addition of excess assembled SNARE complexes in the reaction caused no obvious effect on the FRET between C2B and PI(4,5)P2-containing liposomes (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: The K326 K327 region binds specifically to PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes in the absence of Ca2+.
source: These results, together with a recent finding that Syt1 binds to PI(4,5)P2-containing liposomes in physiological ionic conditions that contain ATP and Mg2+ (Park et al., 2015), suggest that the K326 K327 region binds specifically to PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes in the absence of Ca2+.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and a cited study.

claim: C2B clustered liposomes in response to Ca2+.
source: In our study using PS-containing liposomes, we indeed found that C2B clustered liposomes in response to Ca2+ (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both C2B2RQ and C2b failed to cluster liposomes, while C2B2KE was able to cluster liposomes.
source: Both C2B2RQ and C2b failed to cluster liposomes, while C2B2KE was able to cluster liposomes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), supporting the idea that the bottom R398 R399 region and the top Ca2+-binding loops associate two opposite acidic membranes in response to Ca2+ (Xue et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The bottom R398 R399 region and the top Ca2+-binding loops associate two opposite acidic membranes in response to Ca2+.
source: Both C2B2RQ and C2b failed to cluster liposomes, while C2B2KE was able to cluster liposomes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), supporting the idea that the bottom R398 R399 region and the top Ca2+-binding loops associate two opposite acidic membranes in response to Ca2+ (Xue et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: The addition of 10 μM soluble SNARE complexes strongly impaired liposome clustering but the clustering was capable of gradually recovery as the concentration of C2B exceeded that of SNARE complexes.
source: To our surprise, the addition of 10 μM soluble SNARE complexes in the reaction strongly impaired liposome clustering but the clustering was capable of gradually recovery as the concentration of C2B exceeded that of SNARE complexes (when C2B was above 10 μM, Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The weaker R398 R399–PS interaction can be replaced by the stronger R398 R399–SNARE complex binding.
source: Thus, the likely explanation is that the weaker R398 R399–PS interaction can be replaced by the stronger R398 R399–SNARE complex binding.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The R398 R399 region binds preferentially to SNARE complexes rather than acidic membranes.
source: These results suggest that the R398 R399 region binds preferentially to SNARE complexes rather than acidic membranes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The addition of C2B T285W induced robust quenching of bimane fluorescence on the SNARE complex.
source: In contrast to a donor only condition (no addition of C2B) and the addtion of C2B (WT), the addition of C2B T285W induced robust quenching of bimane fluorescence on the SNARE complex (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: C2B T285W containing the R398Q/R399Q mutation showed strongly impaired binding to the SNARE complex.
source: Comparably, C2B T285W containing the R398Q/R399Q mutation (referred to as T285W2RQ) showed strongly impaired binding to the SNARE complex, whereas C2B T285W containing the K326E/K327E mutation (referred to as T285W2KE) did not have such an effect (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: C2B T285W containing the K326E/K327E mutation did not show impaired binding to the SNARE complex.
source: Comparably, C2B T285W containing the R398Q/R399Q mutation (referred to as T285W2RQ) showed strongly impaired binding to the SNARE complex, whereas C2B T285W containing the K326E/K327E mutation (referred to as T285W2KE) did not have such an effect (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: The specific R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction persists in a physiological ionic environment containing ATP and Mg2+.
source: Robust quenching of bimane fluorescence was still observed with the addition of C2B T285W (Figure 3D,E), suggesting that the specific R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction persists in a physiological ionic environment.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Titration of C2B T285W to liposomes containing bimane-labeled cis-SNARE complexes yielded a Kd of 1.53 ± 0.04 μM in the absence of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Titration of C2B T285W to liposomes containing bimane-labeled cis-SNARE complexes yielded a Kd of 1.53 ± 0.04 μM in the absence of PI(4,5)P2, and a Kd of 0.86 ± 0.04 μM in the presence of PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 4)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Titration of C2B T285W to liposomes containing bimane-labeled cis-SNARE complexes yielded a Kd of 0.86 ± 0.04 μM in the presence of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Titration of C2B T285W to liposomes containing bimane-labeled cis-SNARE complexes yielded a Kd of 1.53 ± 0.04 μM in the absence of PI(4,5)P2, and a Kd of 0.86 ± 0.04 μM in the presence of PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 4)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: There is a rather strong interaction between C2B (R398 R399) and the membrane-anchored cis-SNARE complex when PI(4,5)P2 is present.
source: Titration of C2B T285W to liposomes containing bimane-labeled cis-SNARE complexes yielded a Kd of 1.53 ± 0.04 μM in the absence of PI(4,5)P2, and a Kd of 0.86 ± 0.04 μM in the presence of PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 4), indicating a rather strong interaction between C2B (R398 R399) and the membrane-anchored cis-SNARE complex when PI(4,5)P2 is present.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 helps recruit C2B to the membrane through the K326 K327 region and thereby increases the encounter between the R398 R399 region of C2B and the SNARE complex on membranes.
source: This higher binding affinity arises likely because PI(4,5)P2 helps recruit C2B to the membrane through the K326 K327 region and thereby increases the encounter between the R398 R399 region of C2B and the SNARE complex on membranes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: C2B pre-adsorbs to the plasma membrane prior to Ca2+ influx, through its side K326 K327 region interacting with PI(4,5)P2, and its bottom R398 R399 region binding to surrounding SNAREs or assembled SNARE complexes.
source: It is conceivable that C2B pre-adsorbs to the plasma membrane prior to Ca2+ influx, through its side K326 K327 region interacting with PI(4,5)P2, and its bottom R398 R399 region binding to surrounding SNAREs (e.g., SNAP-25) or assembled SNARE complexes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Efficient binding of C2B to liposomes was only observed when cis-SNARE complexes and PS were both present on liposomes in the presence of 0.1 mM Ca2+.
source: Efficient binding was only observed when cis-SNARE complexes and PS were both present on liposomes in the presence of 0.1 mM Ca2+ (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Inclusion of 1% PI(4,5)P2 on liposomes that already contain PS and cis-SNARE complexes dramatically enhanced C2B binding in the presence of 0.1 mM Ca2+.
source: Intriguingly, inclusion of 1% PI(4,5)P2 on liposomes that already contain PS and cis-SNARE complexes dramatically enhanced C2B binding in the presence of 0.1 mM Ca2+, leaving very little C2B left in the pellet (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Selective removal of PS, PI(4,5)P2 or cis-SNARE complexes on liposomes led to strong impairment of C2B binding.
source: In contrast, selective removal of PS, PI(4,5)P2 or cis-SNARE complexes on liposomes led to strong impairment of C2B binding (Figure 5C,D), suggesting a synergy among the C2B (Ca2+–binding loops)–Ca2+–PS, C2B (K326 K327)–PI(4,5)P2 and C2B (R398 R399)–SNARE complex interactions in the presence of 0.1 mM Ca2+.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: There is a synergy among the C2B (Ca2+–binding loops)–Ca2+–PS, C2B (K326 K327)–PI(4,5)P2 and C2B (R398 R399)–SNARE complex interactions in the presence of 0.1 mM Ca2+.
source: In contrast, selective removal of PS, PI(4,5)P2 or cis-SNARE complexes on liposomes led to strong impairment of C2B binding (Figure 5C,D), suggesting a synergy among the C2B (Ca2+–binding loops)–Ca2+–PS, C2B (K326 K327)–PI(4,5)P2 and C2B (R398 R399)–SNARE complex interactions in the presence of 0.1 mM Ca2+.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Addition of either T285W N333C-NBD or T285W I367C-NBD to liposomes containing PS and cis-SNARE complexes caused a marked increase in intensity in the presence of 1 mM Ca2+.
source: In the presence of 1 mM Ca2+, addition of either T285W N333C-NBD or T285W I367C-NBD to liposomes containing PS and cis-SNARE complexes caused a marked increase in intensity (Figure 6B,C), confirming that the loops insert into membranes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The Ca2+-binding loops of C2B insert into membranes in response to Ca2+.
source: In the presence of 1 mM Ca2+, addition of either T285W N333C-NBD or T285W I367C-NBD to liposomes containing PS and cis-SNARE complexes caused a marked increase in intensity (Figure 6B,C), confirming that the loops insert into membranes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: When additional 1% PI(4,5)P2 was applied, both T285W N333C-NBD and T285W I367C-NBD showed even higher intensities.
source: In contrast, when additional 1% PI(4,5)P2 was applied, both T285W N333C-NBD and T285W I367C-NBD showed even higher intensities (Figure 6D,E), implying that the membrane-insertion ability of the Ca2+-binding loops is enhanced with the assist of the C2B–PI(4,5)P2 interaction.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: The membrane-insertion ability of the Ca2+-binding loops is enhanced with the assist of the C2B–PI(4,5)P2 interaction.
source: In contrast, when additional 1% PI(4,5)P2 was applied, both T285W N333C-NBD and T285W I367C-NBD showed even higher intensities (Figure 6D,E), implying that the membrane-insertion ability of the Ca2+-binding loops is enhanced with the assist of the C2B–PI(4,5)P2 interaction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: The loop 3 located on the same side as the K326 K327 region on C2B is more accessible to membranes.
source: Obviously, compared to T285W N333C-NBD, T285W I367C-NBD exhibited a remarkable enhancement in intensity in response to Ca2+ (Figure 6D,E), suggesting that the loop 3 located on the same side as the K326 K327 region (see Figure 6A) on C2B is more accessible to membranes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: The K326 K327 region of C2B persistently sticks to PI(4,5)P2 on the plasma membrane with the insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops into membranes.
source: These results imply that the K326 K327 region of C2B persistently sticks to PI(4,5)P2 on the plasma membrane with the insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops into membranes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Ca2+-independent pre-adsorption of the K326 K327 region to PI(4,5)P2-harboring membranes helps 'steer' the Ca2+-triggered membrane insertion of Syt1 toward the plasma membrane.
source: This supports the idea that Ca2+-independent pre-adsorption of the K326 K327 region to PI(4,5)P2-harboring membranes helps 'steer' the Ca2+-triggered membrane insertion of Syt1 toward the plasma membrane (Bai et al., 2004).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: The addition of T285W N333C-NBD or T285W I367C-NBD induced robust quenching of bimane fluorescence on membrane-anchored cis-SNARE complexes under all conditions with or without Ca2+ and PI(4,5)P2.
source: The addition of T285W N333C-NBD or T285W I367C-NBD induced robust quenching of bimane fluorescence on membrane-anchored cis-SNARE complexes under all conditions with or without Ca2+ and PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 6F–I), suggesting that the R398 R399 region binds consistently to the membrane-anchored SNARE complex before and after Ca2+ influx.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F–I.

claim: The R398 R399 region binds consistently to the membrane-anchored SNARE complex before and after Ca2+ influx.
source: The addition of T285W N333C-NBD or T285W I367C-NBD induced robust quenching of bimane fluorescence on membrane-anchored cis-SNARE complexes under all conditions with or without Ca2+ and PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 6F–I), suggesting that the R398 R399 region binds consistently to the membrane-anchored SNARE complex before and after Ca2+ influx.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 6F–I.

claim: Crystal structures obtained in the absence and presence of Ca2+ produced the same binding interface that involves residues R398 and R399 between Syt1 and the SNARE complex.
source: Indeed, crystal structures obtained in the absence and presence of Ca2+ produced the same binding interface that involves residues R398 and R399 between Syt1 and the SNARE complex (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: The C2B (R398 R399)–SNARE complex interaction is Ca2+ independent and this interaction persists during insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops into the membrane.
source: Together, these results suggest that the C2B (R398 R399)–SNARE complex interaction is Ca2+ independent and this interaction persists during insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops into the membrane.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Both the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction and the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction persist during entry of the Ca2+-binding loops into membranes with PS.
source: In all, based on the findings that both the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction and the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction persist during entry of the Ca2+-binding loops into membranes with PS, it is conceivable that the three simultaneous interactions of C2B induce membrane deformation in response to Ca2+ (see the Discussion), as suggested by Brunger and colleagues (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The three simultaneous interactions of C2B induce membrane deformation in response to Ca2+.
source: In all, based on the findings that both the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction and the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction persist during entry of the Ca2+-binding loops into membranes with PS, it is conceivable that the three simultaneous interactions of C2B induce membrane deformation in response to Ca2+ (see the Discussion), as suggested by Brunger and colleagues (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: Syt1 C2AB or C2B can promote SNARE-dependent liposome fusion in response to Ca2+ in vitro.
source: It has been widely reported that Syt1 C2AB or C2B can promote SNARE-dependent liposome fusion in response to Ca2+ in vitro (Chapman, 2008; Xue et al., 2008; Martens et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The liposome-clustering ability of C2AB (or C2B) correlated strongly with its activity in promoting SNARE-dependent liposome fusion.
source: However, to what extent the promotion activity of C2AB (or C2B) in vitro reflects the triggering activity of Syt1 in vivo must be interpreted with caution because the liposome-clustering ability of C2AB (or C2B) correlated strongly with its activity in promoting SNARE-dependent liposome fusion (Arac et al., 2006; Hui et al., 2011; Xue et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Poly-D-lysine promoted SNARE-dependent lipid mixing and content mixing in the absence of Ca2+.
source: Consistent with previous observations (Hui et al., 2011), addition of 2 µg/ml poly-D-lysine in the mixtures efficiently induced liposome clustering (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), thereby enhancing SNARE-dependent lipid mixing and content mixing in the absence of Ca2+ (in the presence of 0.2 mM EDTA, Figure 7C,I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C,I.

claim: Complexin-1 inhibited both lipid mixing and content mixing in the presence of poly-D-lysine and in the absence of Ca2+.
source: Complexin-1 inhibited both lipid mixing and content mixing in the presence of poly-D-lysine and in the absence of Ca2+ (Figure 7D,J), whereas further addition of 1 mM Ca2+ at 1500 s triggered both lipid mixing and content mixing (Figure 7E,K).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D,J.

claim: Further addition of 1 mM Ca2+ at 1500 s triggered both lipid mixing and content mixing.
source: Complexin-1 inhibited both lipid mixing and content mixing in the presence of poly-D-lysine and in the absence of Ca2+ (Figure 7D,J), whereas further addition of 1 mM Ca2+ at 1500 s triggered both lipid mixing and content mixing (Figure 7E,K).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E,K.

claim: The triggering activity strictly required C2B instead of C2A.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Gaffaney et al., 2008; Xue et al., 2008), the triggering activity strictly required C2B instead of C2A (Figure 7E,K).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E,K and is consistent with previous studies.

claim: C2B was unable to cluster SNARE-bearing liposomes at a concentration of 0.5 μM in this fusion system.
source: We emphasize that C2B was unable to cluster SNARE-bearing liposomes at a concentration of 0.5 μM in this fusion system (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), and trans-SNARE complexes were mostly assembled at the ready-for-fusion stage arrested by complexin-1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Trans-SNARE complexes were mostly assembled at the ready-for-fusion stage arrested by complexin-1.
source: We emphasize that C2B was unable to cluster SNARE-bearing liposomes at a concentration of 0.5 μM in this fusion system (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), and trans-SNARE complexes were mostly assembled at the ready-for-fusion stage arrested by complexin-1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: SNARE pairing was not obviously promoted during the triggering.
source: In addition, SNARE pairing was not obviously promoted during the triggering (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Leakiness was not detected in SNARE-dependent content mixing in the presence of poly-D-lysine with and without C2AB–Ca2+.
source: Leakiness was not detected in SNARE-dependent content mixing in the presence of poly-D-lysine with and without C2AB–Ca2+ (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B,C), indicating that the real membrane fusion events were observed in our experiments.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3B,C.

claim: The Ca2+-binding sites mutation (C2b) strongly impaired the ability of C2B to trigger both lipid mixing and content mixing in response to Ca2+.
source: We found that the Ca2+-binding sites mutation (C2b) strongly impaired the ability of C2B to trigger both lipid mixing and content mixing in response to Ca2+ (Figure 7F,L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F,L.

claim: C2B2KE or C2B2RQ mutations strongly impaired the ability of C2B to trigger both lipid mixing and content mixing in response to Ca2+.
source: Similar results were obtained when using C2B2KE or C2B2RQ mutations (Figure 7F,L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F,L.

claim: The simultaneous interactions of C2B with the SNARE complex and membranes are crucial for the triggering function of Syt1.
source: These results are consistent with those physiological data in previous studies (Li et al., 2006; Xue et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2015), suggesting that the simultaneous interactions of C2B with the SNARE complex and membranes are crucial for the triggering function of Syt1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: Disrupting the C2A Ca2+-binding sites (D230N/D232N, C2aB) caused a moderate impairment in the lipid mixing and content mixing.
source: We found that disrupting the C2A Ca2+-binding sites (D230N/D232N, C2aB) caused a moderate impairment in the lipid mixing and content mixing, whereas disrupting the C2B Ca2+-binding sites (D363N/D365N, C2Ab) totally abolished the ability of C2AB to trigger fusion (Figure 7G,M).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G,M.

claim: Disrupting the C2B Ca2+-binding sites (D363N/D365N, C2Ab) totally abolished the ability of C2AB to trigger fusion.
source: We found that disrupting the C2A Ca2+-binding sites (D230N/D232N, C2aB) caused a moderate impairment in the lipid mixing and content mixing, whereas disrupting the C2B Ca2+-binding sites (D363N/D365N, C2Ab) totally abolished the ability of C2AB to trigger fusion (Figure 7G,M).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G,M.

claim: Disruption of the Ca2+-binding sites on both C2 domains (D230N/D232N/D363N/D365N, C2ab) completely abolished the triggering effect.
source: Disruption of the Ca2+-binding sites on both C2 domains (D230N/D232N/D363N/D365N, C2ab) completely abolished the triggering effect (Figure 7G,M).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G,M.

claim: This fusion system successfully reconstituted the triggering role of C2AB and C2B in vitro and reproduced the relative importance of the C2 domain Ca2+-binding sites observed in vivo.
source: Thus, this fusion system successfully reconstituted the triggering role of C2AB and C2B in vitro and reproduced the relative importance of the C2 domain Ca2+-binding sites observed in vivo (Mackler et al., 2002; Nishiki and Augustine, 2004; Robinson et al., 2002; Shin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: Syt1AB (WT) and its mutations on the Ca2+-binding sites (Syt1aB, Syt1Ab and Syt1ab, respectively) all stimulated lipid mixing and content mixing in the absence of Ca2+ and complexin-1.
source: We found that Syt1AB (WT) and its mutations on the Ca2+-binding sites (Syt1aB, Syt1Ab and Syt1ab, respectively) all stimulated lipid mixing and content mixing in the absence of Ca2+ and complexin-1 (Figure 8C,F), consistent with the docking role of Syt1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C,F.

claim: Complexin-1 arrested liposomes bearing Syt1 at the ready-for-fusion stage, and further addition of 1 mM Ca2+ at 1500 s triggered fusion.
source: As expected, complexin-1 arrested liposomes bearing Syt1 at the ready-for-fusion stage, and further addition of 1 mM Ca2+ at 1500 s triggered fusion (Figure 8D,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D,G.

claim: Syt1AB and Syt1aB efficiently triggered lipid mixing and content mixing while Syt1Ab and Syt1ab did not.
source: Consistent with the results observed in our C2AB-based fusion experiments (Figure 7), Syt1AB and Syt1aB efficiently triggered lipid mixing and content mixing while Syt1Ab and Syt1ab did not (Figure 8D,E,G,H), verifying the functional importance of the C2B Ca2+-binding sites in Ca2+-triggered liposome fusion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D,E,G,H.

claim: The functional importance of C2B arises most likely from its unique structure that contains abundant basic residues on its surface.
source: The functional importance of C2B arises most likely from its unique structure that contains abundant basic residues on its surface, which endows C2B with the ability to bind acidic SNARE complexes and/or membranes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and structural knowledge.

claim: The presence of PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes shifts the equilibrium towards an energetically favorable binding where the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction dominates.
source: However, as demonstrated with our co-flotation and FRET experiments (Figure 2C–G), the presence of PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes shifts the equilibrium towards an energetically favorable binding where the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction dominates.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 2C–G.

claim: The much higher efficiency of the K326 K327 region, compared to the R398 R399 region, in PI(4,5)P2 binding arises most likely because the K326 K327 region contains a much higher positive-charge density.
source: The much higher efficiency of the K326 K327 region, compared to the R398 R399 region, in PI(4,5)P2 binding arises most likely because the K326 K327 region contains a much higher positive-charge density, which enables it to bind tightly to lipid head groups with a highly negative-charge density [i.e., PI(4,5)P2-microdomains at active zones] (Honigmann et al., 2013; Joung et al., 2012; Park et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from structural knowledge and supported by citations.

claim: The existence of the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction and the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction prior to Ca2+ influx likely recruits Syt1 to the fusion sites.
source: Thus, the existence of the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction and the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction prior to Ca2+ influx likely recruits Syt1 to the fusion sites, which underlies the docking function of Syt1, as suggested previously (de Wit et al., 2009; Honigmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: The R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction persists in the absence and presence of ATP and Mg2+.
source: Instead, our study found that the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction persists in the absence and presence of ATP and Mg2+ (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The interaction between Syt1 and the SNARE complex is not affected by ionic shielding and is physiologically relevant.
source: Thus, our binding results, together with the observations that both spontaneous and Ca2+-evoked release are not affected by the presence of 3 mM ATP (Zhou et al., 2015), strongly suggest that the interaction between Syt1 and the SNARE complex is not affected by ionic shielding and is physiologically relevant.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: The R398 R399–PS binding might be displaced by the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction.
source: This data suggests that the R398 R399–PS binding might be displaced by the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Before Ca2+ influx, both the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction and the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction fasten C2B in an orientation parallel with the plasma membrane, leaving the Ca2+-binding loops held back from membrane insertion.
source: before Ca2+ influx, both the K326 K327–PI(4,5)P2 interaction and the R398 R399–SNARE complex interaction fasten C2B in an orientation parallel with the plasma membrane, leaving the Ca2+-binding loops held back from membrane insertion (Figure 9A)
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data.

claim: Ca2+ influx strongly induces fast insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops into membranes, rearranging C2B to an orientation vertical to the plasma membrane.
source: Ca2+ influx strongly induces fast insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops into membranes, rearranging C2B to an orientation vertical to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data.

claim: The persistent binding of C2B to PI(4,5)P2 and the membrane-anchored SNARE complex would exert a membrane bending force to buck the local membrane outward in response to Ca2+.
source: The persistent binding of C2B to PI(4,5)P2 and the membrane-anchored SNARE complex would thus exert a membrane bending force to buck the local membrane outward in response to Ca2+ (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data.

claim: Binding of C2B to PI(4,5)P2 and SNARE complexes before Ca2+ influx would lead to a ring-like arrangement of C2B molecules around the fusion pore.
source: Furthermore, it is likely that binding of C2B to PI(4,5)P2 and SNARE complexes before Ca2+ influx would lead to a ring-like arrangement of C2B molecules around the fusion pore (Wang et al., 2014), which would then facilitate bucking local membranes upon collective bending forces in response to Ca2+.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental data and a citation.

claim: This possible membrane-deformation mechanism is in good agreement with the Syt1 working model proposed by Brunger and colleagues.
source: This possible membrane-deformation mechanism is in good agreement with the Syt1 working model proposed by Brunger and colleagues (Zhou et al., 2015), and is supported by a recent observation that local membrane protrusions (5 nm in height, similar to the size of one C2B molecule) bucked on the surface of GUV (giant unilamellar vesicles) require the presence of Syt1 and assembled SNARE complexes (Bharat et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: Local membrane protrusions (5 nm in height, similar to the size of one C2B molecule) bucked on the surface of GUV require the presence of Syt1 and assembled SNARE complexes.
source: This possible membrane-deformation mechanism is in good agreement with the Syt1 working model proposed by Brunger and colleagues (Zhou et al., 2015), and is supported by a recent observation that local membrane protrusions (5 nm in height, similar to the size of one C2B molecule) bucked on the surface of GUV (giant unilamellar vesicles) require the presence of Syt1 and assembled SNARE complexes (Bharat et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: The proposed membrane-deformation mechanism explains very well the recent observation that isolated C2B readily bends membranes.
source: The proposed membrane-deformation mechanism is supported by the finding that all three interactions of C2B are required for the triggering function of the Syt1 in liposome fusion (Figure 7). This membrane-deformation mechanism explains very well the recent observation that isolated C2B readily bends membranes (Hui et al., 2009)
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: Membrane insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops alone is not sufficient to drive membrane deformation without the assist of the R398 R399 and the K326 K327 regions.
source: and suggests that membrane insertion of the Ca2+-binding loops alone is not sufficient to drive membrane deformation without the assist of the R398 R399 and the K326 K327 regions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Disruption of the C2B Ca2+-binding sites abrogates the simultaneous interaction of C2B with acidic membrane lipids and the membrane-anchored SNARE complex, so that the ability of C2B to bend membranes is absolutely abolished.
source: Thus, the functional importance of the C2B Ca2+-binding sites observed in previous in vivo studies and our present liposome fusion experiments (Figures 7 and 8) can be explained: disruption of the C2B Ca2+-binding sites abrogates the simultaneous interaction of C2B with acidic membrane lipids [i.e., PI(4,5)P2 and PS] and the membrane-anchored SNARE complex, so that the ability of C2B to bend membranes is absolutely abolished.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Local membrane deformation by Ca2+–Syt1 is key for the triggering function of Syt1 in release.
source: Our data reinforce the idea that local membrane deformation by Ca2+–Syt1 is key for the triggering function of Syt1 in release (Hui et al., 2009; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: The coordinated efforts of two or more interactions from one protein can induce membrane deformation.
source: Our data also reinforce the notion that the coordinated efforts of two or more interactions from one protein can induce membrane deformation (McMahon and Boucrot, 2015).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: SNARE complexes are already partially assembled before Ca2+ influx.
source: The liposome fusion results support the notion that SNARE complexes are already partially assembled before Ca2+ influx (Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2B), which enables complexin-1 binding and thereby strains such a complex in a stage ready for fusion (Rizo and Xu, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: C2B-induced membrane bucking would reduce the distance between two apposed membranes.
source: In response to Ca2+, C2B-induced membrane bucking would reduce the distance between two apposed membranes, which might cooperate with the action of C2B in displacing inhibitory complexin-1, to facilitate the continuous helical SNARE complex assembly that propagates through the linker region into the transmembrane domains (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data.

claim: High curvature stresses induced by C2B and the energy released from the C-terminal SNARE complex assembly might be coupled together in response to Ca2+ to overcome the energy barrier for membrane fusion.
source: Thus, high curvature stresses induced by C2B and the energy released from the C-terminal SNARE complex assembly might be coupled together in response to Ca2+ to overcome the energy barrier for membrane fusion.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data.

claim: C2A would have an ancillary role by binding to one membrane and helping to dictate the apparent Ca2+ affinity of Syt1.
source: It is noteworthy that C2A would have an ancillary role by binding to one membrane and helping to dictate the apparent Ca2+ affinity of Syt1 (Robinson et al., 2002; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data and supported by citations.
